header.description: MLP-neuron DBM on a sparse-MoE layer: two gates at one layer, both trained, both in the swap. routed_gate sits on expert_activation - the routed interior's activated gate half, token-major (top_k slots of d_expert, slot k the k-th ranked expert) - with group expert_neuron, so it holds ONE theta per (expert, neuron): num_experts x d_expert in total, whatever top_k experts a token activates. A slot's coordinates use the parameters of the expert filling it, looked up through expert_idx at the same token; an expert a token did not activate has no slot there and its parameters leave that token alone. shared_gate is the ordinary per-coordinate gate on shared_expert_activation - one parameter per shared-expert neuron, separate keys. Swap under routing mismatch: a base slot holding expert e takes the counterfactual activation of e at the same token when e is active there, and otherwise keeps its base value; the executor records, per layer and example, how many base slots had no counterfactual source, in routing_mismatch.json beside fit_diagnostics.json. The one l1 term names both gates: the mean soft mask over the concatenation of their parameter tables, so one weight counts selected neurons across both and sweeping train.objective.sparsity.weight is the sparsity curve's single axis; fit_diagnostics.json's hard_mask_size counts (expert, neuron) units for routed_gate and neurons for shared_gate. Layer 19 of Qwen3.6-35B-A3B; every layer is a MoE layer, so any layer works. Flat rather than an application of methods/dbm.json because the gate unit, the components and the penalty's meaning all differ from the per-coordinate residual-stream fit. train.eval.split is the held-out validation split; iia.json is the TRAIN score - read train_eval.json for the validation one and dbm_expert_neuron_apply.json for a confirmation replay. As with dbm.json, gate on decisive_fraction before believing a number: the l1 weight below is a starting point, not a tuned one.
